thesis: The episode explores the history of quantitative fixed income, tracing its evolution from the 1974 Lehman Government/Credit Index and the subsequent development of the securitization market to the lessons learned from the 1994 mortgage market meltdown. The discussion highlights how financial crises serve as seminal moments that force a deeper understanding of models and innovations, contrasting this with the limited learning that occurs during complacency periods.
